title.narrative: Research into Ficha Limpa Campaign and production of resources for campaigning

description.narrative: This project will specifically focus on a case study of the Ficha Limpa (“Clean Record”) Campaign. The Ficha Limpa law was the second law of popular initiative to become law in Brazil. Its campaign was promoted by some of the same people that pushed for the first Law 9840 in 1999 that banned vote buying. The campaign put in the hands of civil society a tool to combat the theft of public monies and other criminal activities diverting resources from the poor, so entrenched in the Brazilian political society and one of the root causes of endemic inequality But it also provided a glimpse into a new way of popular participation. Through the mobilisation of citizens over a period of two years, led by the MCCE with our partners CBJP (Brazilian Justice and Peace Commission) as founding members, the Ficha Limpa campaign managed more than 1.6million signatures of the electorate to push for a discussion on the law in congress. At the end of this physical mobilisation a virtual campaign that gathered an extra 400,000 was also launched that together with the lobby of key actors, contributed to pushing the law through congress and pressured for a positive vote on the law. One of the key aspects of the campaign was this joining of classic mobilisation- getting signatures one by one through organisation of church groups at parish level, through community groups, through professional organisations – together with a ‘lightning’ digital mobilisation that managed to inundate the congress with telephone calls, emails, petitions etc through social networks. So wide reaching was this campaign that a recent well respected poll in Brazil showed that a full 85% of the population new what the Ficha Limpa law is. This proposal wishes to undertake a case study of the campaign process that led to the passing of the ficha limpa law-What made this campaign a success? We wish to explore the tactics used by the main protagonists in the campaign and to understand how and where the offline campaign mixed with the online campaign to produce the successful result it did. Results of this study will be produced in an interactive digital format, with recommendations for partners advocacy work. We hope to specifically use this research as part of the capacity building we are doing with both the Economic Justice Programme and the Urban Programme where our focus is on increasing communications capacity for improved advocacy.
